item.title: Ready or not, here come the AI gadgets, from "charms" to smart speakers
item.description: Meta, Microsoft and other major tech companies are developing a range of AI products for consumers, from wearables to speakers.

item.title: Iran proposes a 7-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran's president says Tehran wants a deal with the U.S. before November's midterm elections, as the regime puts an offer on the table.

item.title: Pittsburgh doctor killed while he slept remembered as "a true angel on Earth"
item.description: Dr. Idris Evans, the Pittsburgh doctor killed in a violent home invasion, is being remembered for his kindness and compassion.

item.title: A U.S. doctor survived a deadly strike in Gaza. Why he plans to go back.
item.description: Dr. Feroze Sidhwa was working at Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis when an Israeli strike hit the surgical unit he was in.

item.title: Tasia Fortune's hanging was "staged" after her death, police say
item.description: Authorities haven't disclosed the exact cause of Fortune's death, but they did rule it a homicide and have arrested two men.

item.title: Abraham Accords countries hold first official meeting since Oct. 7 attacks
item.description: Ten blocks away from the United Nations General Assembly​, U.S. diplomats quietly kickstarted the expansion of the Abraham Accords from the 43rd floor of a midtown Manhattan office tower.

item.title: Doctor debunks myths about bone health
item.description: Dr. Jocelyn Wittstein debunked myths about bone health during an episode of "Healthful" with Norah O'Donnell.

item.title: Facebook found liable of deceiving users in Cambridge Analytica case
item.description: The two-week trial in New Mexico centered on accusations Facebook deceived users about a data breach.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Sept. 27)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: An inside look at the rising danger humanitarian aid workers see in combat zones
item.description: According to the U.N., more than 1,000 humanitarian aid workers have been killed in the last three years, while violent incidents affecting aid workers have grown by nearly 1,600% since 2000. CBS News' Lindsey Reiser reports.

item.title: Soaring U.S. diesel prices slam local communities as fuel costs surge
item.description: The surge in diesel prices this year is putting a financial squeeze on schools, farms and small businesses around the U.S.

item.title: Latest on nor'easter track up East Coast, Hurricane Nolo's path toward Hawaii
item.description: Millions are bracing for severe weather this weekend with Hurricane Nolo headed toward Hawaii and a nor'easter bringing dangerous conditions up the East Coast. CBS News' Tom Hanson and Jessica Burch have more.

item.title: Trump-Xi visit wraps with Tillis calling it "a WTF moment"
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping wrapped his visit to Washington, D.C., on Friday, with President Trump getting blowback from outgoing GOP Sen. Thom Tillis for the red-carpet rollout Xi received. CBS News' Weijia Jiang and Anna Coren have more.

item.title: Stanford University apologizes for switching students' faces and races in photo
item.description: Stanford University apologized for what it called a "serious error in judgment," editing a photo of students to alter looks, race and gender. Jonathan Vigliotti reports.

item.title: Trump-Xi visit wraps up with few achievements announced
item.description: President Trump described Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit this week as "very productive," though the White House has said little about what was achieved during the summit.

item.title: James Talarico challenges Ken Paxton to Fox News debate
item.description: Democratic U.S. Senate nominee James Talarico challenged his Republican rival Ken Paxton to a Fox News debate. CBS News' Caitlin Huey-Burns has more.

item.title: Oregon attorney general says "people are incredibly fearful" about election integrity
item.description: Despite no evidence of mass voter fraud, the Trump administration has doubled down on claims that elections are not secure. Dan Rayfield, Oregon's Democratic attorney general, weighs in on election security.

item.title: Supreme Court lets Trump administration use SAVE database for now
item.description: In a 6-3 decision, the Supreme Court sided with the Trump administration in its push to use a controversial database to review state voter rolls for potential noncitizens.

item.title: Minnesota sailor returns from USS Lincoln duty to find apartment ransacked
item.description: A Minnesota native who had been serving aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln for nearly 10 months came home to an upsetting surprise.

item.title: Jane Doe who accused Jay-Z of sexual assault formally recants her claims
item.description: The anonymous woman who accused Jay-Z of sexually assaulting her said in a new court filing that she never met the rap mogul.

item.title: Was Netanyahu's fiery U.N. speech aimed at his own political survival?
item.description: Israel's embattled leader lashed out at New York's mayor in a heated U.N. address, but a veteran analyst says his real targets were Israeli voters and President Trump.

item.title: New Trump-focused "Love Me" ad campaign paid for by taxpayers hits airwaves
item.description: Ads promoting President Trump and paid for by American taxpayers are now airing on network and national cable.

item.title: U.S. military lays groundwork for potential action around Cuba
item.description: Some units would "possibly [be] needed in 90-120 days," according to an internal Army message reviewed by CBS News.

item.title: Hurricane Nolo could cause "catastrophic" flooding in Hawaii, forecasters warn
item.description: A hurricane watch is in effect for Hawaii County due to the storm, which could dump up to 3 feet of rain on Hawaii's Big Island.

item.title: What Happened to Mamta Kafle Bhatt? | Case by Case | "48 Hours" Podcast
item.description: Mamta Kafle Bhatt vanished without a trace in 2024. Ahead of trial, "48 Hours" producer Michelle Sigona and "48 Hours" consultant Herman Weisberg explore the evidence prosecutors say points to her husband, Naresh Bhatt, and what jurors may hear in this closely watched no-body case.

item.title: Mistress testifies in trial of "American Idol" contestant charged in wife's murder
item.description: Caleb Flynn, a former "American Idol" contestant, is charged with killing his wife Ashley Flynn in February and then staging the crime scene.

item.title: 9/24: CBS Evening News
item.description: Trump hosts Xi Jinping at White House; Sen. Thom Tillis on elaborate Trump-Xi visit.

item.title: DSA candidate Angie Nixon says "this is not about three letters"
item.description: Florida Democratic Senate nominee Angie Nixon, a state representative, said that "this is not about three letters" amid GOP criticism about her membership in the Democratic Socialists of America.

item.title: Florida gov. candidate Byron Donalds responds after Trump mentions removed from site
item.description: Some prominent references to President Trump were scrubbed from Florida gubernatorial candidate Byron Donalds' campaign website in recent weeks, but the Republican said he isn't backing away from the president's agenda.

item.title: Sen. Tim Scott says GOP in "fight for our lives," sees path to holding Senate
item.description: With just under six weeks until the midterms, Sen. Tim Scott of South Carolina laid out the NRSC's strategy to try to hold onto the Senate amid a tough political environment.
